newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.81 pct in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.81 pct in quiet trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose slightly in quiet and selective trade on Friday with the help of support awaited at around the index's 1,600 level, despite caution which persisted due to ongoing political tension, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed up 13 points, or 0.81 percent at 1,612, after rebounding from an early low of 1,587. Trade volume slipped to 16.78 trillion lira ($137 million) from 17.15 trillion ($140.4 million) on Thursday.

"Political tension depressed the market since the start of this week. A wait-and-see attitude was kept today. The index cannot gather enough strength for a rise. It may try an upward move next week," said Soner Canoglu from Yasar investment.
A National Security Council (NSC) meeting anxiously awaited by market players began at 1310 GMT.

Top political leaders and military commanders met for talks chaired by President Suleyman Demirel and expected to focus on increasing strains between the Islamist-led government and the secular establishment.
Over the week, the index lost only three points, compared to last week's 3.86 percent gain.
